column1: # Frames of one gamepad slot, and whether the slot counts as a controller after each of them. Both rules read this
# file: PollGamepads() with HasGamepadInputChanged() in wasm/gamepad.cpp, which decides what the stream announces to the
# PC (tests/native/gamepad_evidence_test.cpp), and Controller.isRealGamepad() in wasm/platform/gamepad.js, which decides
# what the menus, System information, the input test, the button mapping and the mask of a stream start count
# (tests/unit/gamepad-js.test.js), so the two stay the same.
# A slot counts with a positive timestamp, or once its input changed since it appeared: a button whose pressed state
# flipped, or a button value or axis that moved more than 0.01 away from its first value. A static value never counts.
# This tells the placeholder slots of Tizen, which report a timestamp of 0 and never change, from the controllers of
# Tizen 5.5, which report a timestamp of 0 too (upstream fdf4fbe, PR #192 by podrezov).
# Format: a name, a tab, one character per frame (1 if the slot counts after that frame, 0 if not), a tab, the frames
# separated by spaces. A frame is timestamp/buttons/axes, or timestamp/buttons/axes/id: the buttons and the axes as
# values separated by commas, a button with a * after its value when it is pressed, and nan for a value that is not a
# number. The id is Pad unless a frame gives one. A frame of - is an empty slot.
# A positive timestamp counts at once, and the evidence stays for the id
a positive timestamp counts at once
a timestamp that reads 0 later keeps the controller
a negative or missing timestamp needs input like 0
# Placeholders: a static slot never counts, also with a held button or an axis off-centre
a static placeholder never counts
a placeholder with a held button and an axis at 0.3 never counts
# The input of a controller with a timestamp of 0 counts, and the evidence stays while the id stays
a press counts
a pressed state that flips without a value change counts
a button held since the slot appeared counts on its release
a stick move of more than 0.01 counts
a move of exactly 0.01 does not count, of a stick or a trigger
jitter of 0.009 around the resting value doesn't count, 0.011 does
a slow move adds up against the first value
a trigger value counts without a pressed state
a value that is not a number takes the first number as its baseline
a button value that is not a number does the same
another button or axis count takes a new baseline without counting
# Another controller in the slot, and a disconnect, need new evidence
another id in the slot needs evidence of its own, measured from its first frame
another id with a positive timestamp counts at once
a disconnect forgets the evidence
